truths.truth: git.auto_close resolves as two named booleans from two sources, and the AUTHORIZED value never comes from a bare `config.mjs get`
truths.evidence: cadence-core/bin/lib/repo-auto-close.mjs is a raw JSON.parse of <dir>/.planning/config.json, fail-closed, and is the ONLY source of the authorized value: a tree-wide grep for repoAutoClose finds exactly two callsites, cadence-core/bin/git-publish.mjs:135 (publish) and :249 (authorized). The requested value comes from the merged read at git-publish.mjs:110-113 (`autoCloseRequested`), extending the existing readProtectedBranches mergeLayers callsite rather than adding one. Live trace of one value end to end on a divergent pair (global true / repo unset): `git-publish.mjs authorized --dir <fx>` printed {"ok":false,"reason":"auto-close-off","requested":true,...} exit 1, and with the repo layer set to true printed {"ok":true,"action":"repo-authorized","requested":true} exit 0. cadence-core/bin/repo-auto-close.test.mjs covers all six cases (repo true/false, key absent, file absent, truncated JSON, global-only); cadence-core/bin/config-seams.test.mjs:545-608 asserts requested true / authorized false on one fixture plus the repo-layer contrast.

truths.truth: The skipped-ask / halt pairing still reads one merged value, and a test goes red if the ask is repointed
truths.evidence: cadence-core/bin/config-seams.test.mjs:572-579 asserts on the divergent pair that `config.mjs get git.auto_close` reports true and that `land-cleanup.mjs gate` still halts with reason /auto_close on/ on a surviving blocker. The call-site half is pinned in cadence-core/bin/prose-agreement.test.mjs ('cad-land step 3: the auto_close branch takes its value from `config.mjs get`'), which asserts step 3's branch region does NOT contain a raw `.planning/config.json` read nor `git-publish.mjs" authorized` - so repointing SKILL.md's ask at the repo layer goes red. Both arms pass in the run of `node --test cadence-core/bin/prose-agreement.test.mjs` (20/20) and the full suite.

truths.truth: The GitLab arm has an authorization answer it consults, it refuses with no forge CLI spawned, and neither doc surface still exempts GitLab
truths.evidence: cadence-core/bin/git-publish.test.mjs:318-345 ('authorized: the GitLab arm refuses with NO forge CLI spawned at all') writes gh/glab/tea stubs onto the child PATH with CAD_SPAWN_MARKER set, asserts the auto-close-off refusal and existsSync(marker) === false, then runs a stub directly to prove the absence is not vacuous. `grep -rn "no seam call is needed" skills/ cadence-core/` matches only the guard assertion inside prose-agreement.test.mjs:794. skills/cad-land/SKILL.md:139-151 now runs `git-publish.mjs authorized --dir <root>` ahead of the whole Open/reuse bullet; cadence-core/references/git-publish.md:24-27 restates the rule. prose-agreement.test.mjs pins ORDER, not presence: seamAt < createAt AND seamAt < viewAt (the reuse probe), so a consult moved after either goes red.

truths.truth: The refusal envelope names WHICH authorization was missing, from one core, with reason unchanged
truths.evidence: authorizationDetail at cadence-core/bin/lib/publish-decision.mjs:54-65 is pure and total, returns null when authorized, and returns two distinct sentences; decidePublish gate 1 (:113-116) is the only refusal carrying a detail, and the JSDoc gate ladder (:72-75) states it. publish-decision.test.mjs:69-124 asserts the two details differ, that the requested-globally sentence says a user-global setting cannot authorize and names .planning/config.json, that gate 1 is the ONLY refusal with a detail, and that a bare call still words itself. Observed live: the authorized subcommand emitted reason auto-close-off with the requested-globally sentence.

truths.truth: On GitLab, an actual unattended run cannot reach `glab mr create`/`glab mr merge` without the repo-layer boolean
truths.evidence: The enforcement on the GitLab arm is prose (skills/cad-land/SKILL.md step 3(b)) plus prose-agreement.test.mjs reading that prose - there is no runtime interlock: cadence-core/bin/land-cleanup.mjs does not refuse to proceed when the consult was skipped, so a model that departs from step 3(b) still reaches `glab mr merge`. SUMMARY.md:83-89 states this limit honestly. The ROADMAP's own success criterion 3 asks for a test showing the GitLab path refusing, which truth 3 satisfies; what no probe here can settle is the live-agent behaviour, and `glab` is absent on this machine with no GitLab remote to run against.

human_checks.name: Walk /cad-land step 3(b) on a real GitLab repository whose .planning/config.json never sets git.auto_close while the user-global layer sets it to true, once with an MR already open for the branch and once with none.
human_checks.expected: In both runs the agent runs `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/cadence-core/bin/git-publish.mjs" authorized --dir <root>` before it touches the remote, gets ok:false, and stops - no `glab mr view`, no `glab mr create`, no `glab mr merge` - surfacing the detail sentence about a user-global setting not authorizing this repository.
human_checks.why_human: Out-of-reach resource plus live-agent behaviour: `glab` is absent on this machine and there is no GitLab remote to run against, and the GitLab enforcement is prose rather than a runtime interlock (land-cleanup.mjs does not refuse a merge whose consult was skipped), so no probe in the repo can observe whether a real run honours the ordering. The seam-level and prose-level pins are already verified (truth 3); this is the only remaining claim they cannot reach.
